insider_note: This answer is a list of numbers: 300 nm, 18 nm, 2130 capsomeres, 158 amino acids, 6500 nucleotides, 4 nm core. Write every one you remember — each is worth credit.

steps.label: What TMV is
steps.margin_note: Expansion, host, symptom, nucleic acid type. Five lines.
lines: TMV stands for TOBACCO MOSAIC VIRUS.
It is a plant virus that infects tobacco plants
and causes a mosaic pattern of light and dark
patches on the leaves.
It is a single stranded RNA virus.
It was the FIRST virus ever discovered.
steps.why: TMV was the first virus isolated and the first whose structure was worked out, which is why it is the standard example in every syllabus.
common_mistakes: Saying TMV is a DNA virus. Its genetic material is single stranded RNA.
Saying it infects animals. TMV is a PLANT virus.

steps.label: Shape and size
steps.margin_note: Shape and both numbers. The molecular weight is a bonus.
lines: TMV is ROD SHAPED.
It is about 300 nm long and 18 nm in diameter.
Its molecular weight is about 39 million
daltons (39 x 10 to the power 6).
steps.why: The rod shape follows from the helical arrangement of its capsomeres, so shape and internal structure are the same fact described twice.
common_mistakes: Calling TMV spherical. It is ROD shaped.
Swapping the two dimensions. 300 nm is the LENGTH; 18 nm is the diameter.
steps.memory_tip: Three hundred long, eighteen across: a long thin rod.

steps.label: The capsid
steps.margin_note: Number, arrangement, core width, subunit size. All four numbers count.
lines: The capsid is made of 2,130 protein subunits
called CAPSOMERES.
The capsomeres are arranged in a HELICAL manner
around a central hollow core of 4 nm.
Each protein subunit is made of 158 amino
acids.
steps.why: A helical stack of identical subunits is what makes a rod rather than a sphere, so the arrangement explains the shape given in the step above.
common_mistakes: Saying the capsomeres are arranged in a sphere. They are HELICAL.
Leaving out the hollow core. The 4 nm channel runs down the middle.
steps.memory_tip: Two thousand one hundred and thirty bricks, wound in a helix.

steps.label: The RNA core
steps.margin_note: Strandedness, the coil, the nucleotide count, and what is infective.
lines: Inside the capsid lies a SINGLE STRANDED RNA,
spirally coiled along the hollow core.
It has about 6,500 nucleotides.
The RNA is the infective part: it alone can
infect a tobacco plant.
steps.why: The RNA follows the same helix as the protein, so the coat and the genome are wound together rather than the genome sitting loose inside.
common_mistakes: Saying the RNA is double stranded. TMV RNA is SINGLE stranded.
Saying the protein is the infective part. The RNA alone can infect.
steps.memory_tip: The RNA follows the same spiral as the coat.

steps.label: Diagram — TMV
steps.margin_note: No diagram mark — the question says 'explain'. Sketch it anyway; the hollow core and the coil are two of the four written marks and the drawing fixes both.

elements.caption: Step 1 — the stack of protein discs
Step 2 — the hollow core down the middle
Step 3 — the single RNA strand coiled inside

steps.why: The drawing makes one point the words cannot: the RNA and the protein subunits follow the same helix, so the coat and the genome are wound together.
common_mistakes: Drawing TMV as a sphere. It is a ROD.
Drawing the RNA as a straight line down the middle. It is SPIRALLY coiled.
Drawing a solid rod with no hollow core. The 4 nm channel runs the whole length.
steps.memory_tip: A stack of discs with a hole down the middle and a coil inside it.
